chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who treads upon excrement or urine, should he repeat the ablution? He said: No, but he should wash what it hit. And in another report: If it is dry, he does not wash it.
ai.seo_question: Does stepping on feces or urine invalidate wudu in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-asl al-salah* (presumption of validity) in ritual purity, distinguishing between the invalidation of wudu and the removal of physical impurity (*kaffar al-najasah*). The distinction between wet and dry impurities reflects the juristic consensus that dryness prevents the transfer of impurity, thereby simplifying the purification process for daily prayers. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the practical application of cleanliness without imposing undue hardship (*la haraj*).
